tables.name: accounts
tables.description: How a person on the business side signs in, one row per person across every business: the owner's one mobile, proven by their own text to Rosie's number (C9), and the owner's email, proven by a code typed on the page (B12, B13; S1-10). Owners, admins and staff sign in by a code to the phone or email on file, with no password (FS section 8; S11-52). The person, the handles and the phone rows are K-04 core's; this row only says which of them is the sign-in and when each was proven.
tables.source: FS rows B11 to B13; FS section 8 ('Owner and staff log in by a code sent to the phone or email on file'); S1-10 (gives mobile); S11-52; S13-45 rows 8 and 9; MC C9; 02-contracts section 8 (mobile: K-04 phone row and K-22)

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: The person who signs in (persons.id); one account per person, for every company (S1-10: 'Done once, for every company').
columns.source: S1-10; FS line 743 (a person is one row)

columns.name: mobile
columns.description: The one mobile only they use, their sign-in (B12), as core's phones.number. Never the listing's number. Texts and pages say 'on file', never the number (S2-06). Null: none given yet.
columns.source: FS row B12 ('the one only they use; it is their sign-in; never the listing's number'); S1-10 ('Never suggest the number on the card or the listing'); S2-06 ('Texts say on file, never a number')

columns.name: mobile_proven_at
columns.description: When the mobile was proven: by the person's own text from it to Rosie's number, since no code is texted to a mobile that has not texted in (C9). Null: not proven, so it is not the sign-in yet.
columns.source: MC C9 ('A code meant for a mobile that has not texted in: Rosie asks them to text from that mobile instead, since that text proves it'); S1-10 (gives mobile); 02-contracts section 8 (mobile: proven by their own text)

columns.name: email
columns.description: The owner's one email for notices, sign-in help and answers by email (B13), in lower case, as a core handles.address. Null: none given.
columns.source: FS row B13; S1-10 ('The secure page also asks one owner email, for notices, sign-in recovery and answers by email'); S13-32

columns.name: email_proven_at
columns.description: When a code sent to the email was typed back on the page (a proof_codes row of purpose owner_email). Until then it is not used.
columns.source: S1-10 ('The email is proven with a code sent to it, typed on the page. Until then it isn't used'); FS row B13

rowLevelSecurity.why: One sign-in per person across every business (S1-10 'Done once, for every company'; S11-52 'every booking for both businesses'), as K-04's persons.

tables.name: id_uploads
tables.description: An ID document the person uploaded on the secure page, never in the chat (C10). Any document is accepted as given, with no check, and a sign_up upload counts as 'the ID confirmed' wherever the master asks for it (S1-10 gives id_checked; S1-32). No face match or video check runs, so no face data is kept. A re_check upload is S13-45 row 8's ID re-check (a new owner mobile or email, a new device, a hand-over). The file stays private in R2 (Q-31); its object key is sealed under the person's key.
tables.source: MC C10; S1-10 (gives id_checked); S1-32; S13-45 row 8; S11-100; FS row B14; RULES 9.5; Q-31; 02-contracts section 5 K-19 and section 8 (id_checked: K-22)

columns.name: id
columns.description: The upload's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).
columns.source: CQ-09 (other ids are opaque strings)

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: The person whose ID it is (persons.id), and whose key seals the file's key.

columns.name: purpose
columns.description: sign_up: the ID at sign-up, done once for every company, which counts as the ID confirmed (S1-10; C10); re_check: the ID re-check S13-45 row 8 asks for a new owner mobile or email, a new device or a hand-over.
columns.source: S1-10 ('Done once, for every company'); S13-45 row 8 ('the ID re-check'); S11-100; RULES 9.5

columns.name: object_key
columns.description: The uploaded file's object key in R2 (K-13), sealed under the person's key, so deleting the key erases the way to the file. Seen only on the secure page; never in a text, an email or a summary.
columns.source: MC C10 ('Uploads stay private in R2'); MC 8 'Files'; Q-31; RULES 4.5 (ID numbers stay on the secure page), 4.10; arch 01 line 93

columns.name: content_type
columns.description: The file's media type: a photo (image/...) or a file such as a PDF (application/...).
columns.source: MC C10 ('a photo or file of an ID document')

columns.name: uploaded_at
columns.description: When it was uploaded; the go-live gate reads it as the ID half of S1-32.
columns.source: MC C10; S1-32; S1-10 ('The result comes back at S1-32')

unique.source: S1-10 ('Checks the owner's mobile and ID, once'; 'Done once, for every company')

indexes.name: id_uploads_person_idx
indexes.why: Whether a person's ID is confirmed (S1-32's gate) and their latest re-check (S13-45 row 8).

tables.name: staff
tables.description: A team member at one business (FS staff row): their mobile, the owner's yes that they agreed to a text, their status (invited, joined, stopped, removed), languages, day-list time, video link or 'the pro calls', supervisor, and when the owner let them take bookings. The person and their name are K-04 core's persons row and their role (owner, admin, staff, own business) is core's person_roles row; a role that ends (removed) keeps core's ended_at. Skills are staff_skills, what they may OK team_powers, on call on_call, an emergency contact emergency_contacts. A price by person (T06) is K-25's, a calendar link K-27's, a license K-35's.

tables.name: emergency_contacts
tables.description: The one person a pro who works alone names for their safety (T11): a solo owner on S1-70's page (S1-78), or a team member on their secure page where their work uses a check-out timer (S2-06). The page asks the contact's name and mobile and a tick that they agreed; both are sealed under the pro's key. The contact is on file only once their own yes comes by texting Rosie (S1-78; Q-06); until then, or with none, no safety timer runs (K-34's safety_timers copy the yes). A STOP or removal ends their yes (S13-10).

columns.name: contact_handle_id
columns.description: The handle the contact's own text came from (handles.id); the timer's alerts and the one address after a missed check go there.
columns.source: Q-06 ('The timer runs only with an emergency contact who said yes by texting Rosie'); S13-10; K-34 v1 safety_timers.emergency_contact_handle_id

columns.name: contact_yes_at
columns.description: When the contact's own yes came; only then is a contact on file and may a timer run. The Team page shows who has one (S2-21), and anyone without one is named on S2-22's card.
columns.source: S1-78 ('Until that yes, no contact is on file'); Q-06; S2-21 ('Safety contact shows who has an emergency contact'); S2-22; K-34 v1 safety_timers.contact_yes_at

columns.name: contact_no_at
columns.description: When the contact said no; no contact is on file, and the pro is told plainly.
columns.source: S1-78 ('Reply 1 Yes, 2 No'; 'With none ... the pro is told plainly')

columns.name: ended_at
columns.description: When their yes ended or the pro replaced or removed them; null while it holds.
columns.source: S13-10 ('An emergency contact's STOP or removal ends their yes. No timer runs')

columns.name: ended_why
columns.description: stop: the contact's STOP; removed: the pro removed them; replaced: the pro named another.
columns.source: S13-10; S1-78 ('Add one any time')

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; arch 10 line 506; K-04 v1 rule 2

unique.name: emergency_contacts_one_live
unique.source: S1-78 ('names one person Rosie may call for their safety')

checks.name: emergency_contacts_not_the_pro
checks.expression: contact_person_id is null or contact_person_id <> person_id
checks.source: S1-78 ('names one person Rosie may call for their safety'; 'We can't reach Sam ... Can you check on them?'); K-34 v1 README ('The contact is not the pro')

checks.name: emergency_contacts_contact_with_handle
checks.source: Q-06 (the yes comes by texting Rosie)

checks.name: emergency_contacts_answer_from_contact
checks.expression: (contact_yes_at is null and contact_no_at is null) or contact_handle_id is not null
checks.source: S1-78 ('Rosie texts the contact once for their own yes'); Q-06

checks.name: emergency_contacts_one_answer
checks.expression: contact_yes_at is null or contact_no_at is null

checks.name: emergency_contacts_ended_has_why
checks.expression: (ended_at is null) = (ended_why is null) and (ended_why is null or ended_why in ('stop', 'removed', 'replaced'))

checks.name: emergency_contacts_times_in_order
checks.expression: added_at >= agreed_ticked_at and (contact_yes_at is null or contact_yes_at >= agreed_ticked_at) and (ended_at is null or ended_at >= added_at)
checks.source: S1-78 ('Never: text the contact before the owner says they agreed')

indexes.name: emergency_contacts_contact_handle_idx
indexes.why: A contact's STOP ends every yes given from that handle (S13-10).

tables.name: proof_codes
tables.description: Each code Rosie sends to prove a contact (RULES 6.1, 6.2; S13-45): a sign-in code, the owner email's code, a new device's code, a contact change's code (D75, D77, D100), the listing's control code (S13-45 row 10), the fresh code before closing or an export, the new owner's code at a hand-over, or the code that lets a phone link to an old record. Never the code itself (rule 7): only its keyed hash. A code works 10 minutes; five wrong codes pause it 15 minutes (RULES 6.2). Rosie never asks for a code by text or call.
tables.source: RULES 6.1, 6.2, 6.5, 6.9, 6.10, 9.1, 9.2, 9.2b; S13-45 (rows 3, 8, 10); S11-52; S1-10; FS section 8; BP rule 7; 02-contracts section 7 row K-22 ('proof codes (10 minutes, 5 tries: RULES 6.2)')

columns.name: id
columns.description: The code row's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).
columns.source: CQ-09 (other ids are opaque strings)

columns.name: purpose
columns.description: sign_in (S11-52), owner_email (S1-10), new_device (S13-45 row 8), contact_change (D75, D77, D100; FS section 8 for staff), listing_control (S13-45 row 10; S1-75), closing_or_export (S13-45 row 8's fresh code to the owner's phone), hand_over (S11-100: the new owner's own phone), link_record (S13-45: before a phone links to an old record).

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: The person the code proves (persons.id); null for a listing's control code, which proves a business.
columns.source: S13-45 ('a code is sent to the contact on file'); S1-75

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The business the code's text names ('Your Lee's Barbershop code is 4829'); null for a sign-in code, which covers every business of the person.
columns.source: S13-45 (the code text); S11-52; S1-75

columns.name: sent_to_handle_id
columns.description: Where the code went (handles.id): the contact on file, or for a contact change the new phone or email (D75), or the email on file when the phone was lost (D100).
columns.source: RULES 9.1, 9.2b; S13-45 row 3 ('The code goes only to the new contact, never the old one'); FS section 8

columns.name: channel
columns.description: text or email. No code is texted to a mobile that has not texted Rosie (C9), and there are no calls (Q-05).
columns.source: MC C9; FS section 8; Q-05

columns.name: code_hash
columns.description: The code's HMAC-SHA-256 under the Workers secret named in hash_key_name, in lowercase hex; never the code (rule 7). A typed code is checked by hashing it the same way.
columns.source: BP rule 7; RULES 6.2 ('Rosie never asks for a code'); arch 09 line 492 (proofs survive as hashes)

columns.name: hash_key_name
columns.description: The name of the Workers secret the hash is keyed with: a name, never a value.
columns.source: BP rule 7; arch 10 line 546 (secrets in Workers secrets); K-04 v1 sealing_keys.wrapping_key_name

columns.name: sent_at
columns.description: When the code was sent.
columns.source: RULES 6.2

columns.name: expires_at
columns.description: When it stops working: 10 minutes after it was sent.
columns.source: RULES 6.2 ('A code works 10 minutes'); S11-52 ('It works for 10 minutes')

columns.name: wrong_tries
columns.description: Wrong codes typed for it, 0 to 5.
columns.source: RULES 6.2 ('Five wrong codes pause it 15 minutes'); S11-52

columns.name: last_wrong_at
columns.description: When the last wrong code was typed; null with no wrong try.
columns.source: RULES 6.2

columns.name: paused_until
columns.description: Set at the fifth wrong code: 15 minutes after it, during which no code for this purpose and contact is sent or taken.
columns.source: RULES 6.2; S11-52 ('Five wrong codes pause sign-in for 15 minutes'); S13-45

columns.name: used_at
columns.description: When the right code was typed back, within its 10 minutes; a code works once.
columns.source: RULES 6.1, 6.2

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; arch 10 line 506; K-04 v1 rule 2

checks.name: proof_codes_who
checks.expression: person_id is not null or (purpose = 'listing_control' and business_id is not null)
checks.source: S13-45 rows 1 to 10 (a code proves a person, or at sign-up a business)

checks.name: proof_codes_wrong_tries_range
checks.expression: wrong_tries between 0 and 5 and (wrong_tries = 0) = (last_wrong_at is null)

checks.name: proof_codes_pause_after_five
checks.expression: (wrong_tries = 5) = (paused_until is not null) and (paused_until is null or paused_until = last_wrong_at + interval '15 minutes')
checks.source: RULES 6.2 ('Five wrong codes pause it 15 minutes')

checks.name: proof_codes_used_in_time
checks.expression: used_at is null or (used_at >= sent_at and used_at <= expires_at and wrong_tries < 5)
checks.source: RULES 6.2 ('A code works 10 minutes'; five wrong codes pause it)

indexes.name: proof_codes_sent_to_idx
indexes.why: The live code for a contact, its pause, and 'at most a few codes a day per contact' (S13-45).

rowLevelSecurity.why: Codes are sent, typed back and checked on the runtime side only, across businesses (a sign-in covers every business: S11-52); the Tool API role has no grant on this table, so no business reads a hash (README rule 5; BP rule 7).

tables.name: sessions
tables.description: A signed-in session on the owner's and staff's portal (S11-52 gives signed_in): who, how the sign-in was proven, a hash of the session token (never the token: rule 7), a hash of the device's id so a new device is known (S13-45 row 8), when it started, was last seen and expires, and when and why it ended. A new owner mobile or email needs a signed-in session plus the ID re-check (S13-45 row 8); someone who leaves loses sign-in (RULES 8.7).
tables.source: S11-52 (gives signed_in); FS section 8; S13-45 row 8; RULES 6.9, 8.7, 9.5; BP rule 7; 02-contracts section 7 row K-22 ('sign-in sessions (S11-52)') and section 8 (signed_in: K-22)

columns.name: id
columns.description: The session's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09); not the token.
columns.source: CQ-09 (other ids are opaque strings)

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: Who signed in (persons.id): an owner, admin or staff member; customers have no login (FS section 8).
columns.source: S11-52; FS section 8 ('Customers have no login and no password')

columns.name: token_sha256
columns.description: The sha256 of the session token, in lowercase hex. The token itself lives only with the signed-in browser and is never stored.
columns.source: BP rule 7 (never a key or token); S11-52

columns.name: device_sha256
columns.description: The sha256 of the device's own id, in lowercase hex, so a sign-in from a device not seen before asks the extra proof (a code to the owner's email typed back, or the ID re-check). Null: not known.
columns.source: S13-45 row 8 ('A new device needs a code to the owner's email, typed back, or the ID re-check'); S11-52 ('A new device ... follows the business side of S13-45'); BP rule 7

columns.name: proven_via
columns.description: code: a sign-in code to the phone or email on file, typed back (S11-52); code_and_email_code: plus a code to the owner's email for a new device; code_and_id_re_check: plus the ID re-check.
columns.source: S11-52; S13-45 row 8; FS section 8

columns.name: proof_code_id
columns.description: The sign-in code it was proven by (proof_codes.id).
columns.source: S11-52 ('Sam types his mobile, and a code comes by text')

columns.name: started_at
columns.description: When it started.

columns.name: last_seen_at
columns.description: When it was last used.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.description: When it stops working unless ended first. Its length is a setting, not in the sources (README open gaps).
columns.source: S11-52; README open gaps

columns.name: ended_at
columns.description: When it ended before expiring; null while live or once expired.
columns.source: RULES 8.7; RULES 9.1 ('the way apps sign out old sessions')

columns.name: ended_why
columns.description: signed_out; contact_changed (the sign-in mobile or email changed: old sessions sign out, as D75 says of links); left (the person left the team or lost the role: RULES 8.7); handed_over (the business changed owner: S11-100).

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; arch 10 line 506; K-04 v1 rule 2

checks.name: sessions_times_in_order
checks.expression: last_seen_at >= started_at and expires_at > started_at and (ended_at is null or ended_at >= started_at)

checks.name: sessions_ended_has_why
checks.expression: (ended_at is null) = (ended_why is null) and (ended_why is null or ended_why in ('signed_out', 'contact_changed', 'left', 'handed_over'))

indexes.name: sessions_person_idx
indexes.why: End a person's sessions when their sign-in contact changes or they leave (RULES 8.7, 9.1).

rowLevelSecurity.why: A session covers every business of the person (S11-52: 'every booking for both businesses') and is read on the runtime side only; the Tool API role has no grant on this table, so no business reads a token hash (README rule 5; BP rule 7).

tables.name: contact_changes
tables.description: A change of where a person's updates go (D75, D77, D100; RULES 9.1 to 9.3; S13-45 row 3), or of an owner's or staff member's own phone or email on file (S13-45 row 8; FS section 8): the old and new contact, the way it was proven, the code or ID re-check that proved it, who made it and when. Never edited; the old contact stays on record only for the 'don't text me' proof, and owner and staff views show the new contact only, with 'Contact details changed.' (FS line 756; RULES 9.3). The two consent rows a switch adds are K-29's.
tables.source: FS line 756 ('a contact switched (D75) adds a consent and a contact change'); FS section 8; RULES 9.1, 9.2, 9.2b, 9.3; S13-45 rows 3, 8; S13-19; A7-98; D75, D77, D100; 02-contracts section 7 row K-22 ('contact changes (D75, D77, D100; FS section 8)')

columns.name: id
columns.description: The change's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).
columns.source: CQ-09 (other ids are opaque strings)

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: The person whose contact it is (persons.id); staff change a contact only for that person (RULES 9.3).
columns.source: RULES 9.3 ('Staff change a contact only for the person whose contact it is'); S13-45 row 3

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The business whose desk or team page made it (in person, D77; the owner's team edit, S11-20); null for a change from the person's own chat or sign-in, which covers every business (one number: D102).
columns.source: D77 ('Staff updating a customer's details in person'); FS section 8 (the owner's team edit, S11-20); D102

columns.name: old_handle_id
columns.description: The contact updates went to before (handles.id); after the change it is never messaged again, and it comes off every owner and staff view (S13-19).
columns.source: RULES 9.1 ('Rosie never messages the old number again'); S13-19; FS line 756 ('the old number stays on record only for the don't text me proof')

columns.name: new_handle_id
columns.description: The new phone or email (handles.id) every update goes to from now on.
columns.source: RULES 9.1

columns.name: way
columns.description: own_chat: asked in the person's own chat and proven by a code to the new contact typed back there (D75); email_on_file: a lost phone, proven by a code to the email on file typed back in the new chat (D100); in_person: at the desk, by a code to the new contact read or typed there (D77); own_code: a staff member's own change by a code to the phone or email on file (FS section 8); signed_in_id_re_check: an owner's new mobile or email from a signed-in session plus the ID re-check (S13-45 row 8); owner_team_edit: the owner's edit of a team member's contact, read back first (S11-20). No reason is asked or shown.
columns.source: D75; D77; D100; RULES 9.1 to 9.3; FS section 8; S13-45 rows 3, 8; S11-20

columns.name: proof_code_id
columns.description: The code that proved it (proof_codes.id), for every way but the ID re-check and the owner's team edit.
columns.source: D75 ('Rosie sends a code there; they type the code back in this chat'); D77; D100

columns.name: id_upload_id
columns.description: The ID re-check that proved an owner's new mobile or email (id_uploads.id).
columns.source: S13-45 row 8 ('A new owner mobile or email only from a signed-in session plus the ID re-check')

columns.name: changed_by_person_id
columns.description: Who made it (persons.id): the person themselves, the staff member at the desk, or the owner for a team edit.
columns.source: D77; RULES 9.3; S2-21 ('Every change shows who made it')

columns.name: changed_at
columns.description: When it took effect. Owner and staff views show only the note 'Contact details changed.' with the new contact.
columns.source: RULES 9.3 ('Owner and staff views then show the new contact only, with one note: Contact details changed.')

checks.name: contact_changes_way_known
checks.source: D75; D77; D100; FS section 8; S13-45 row 8; S11-20

checks.name: contact_changes_new_contact
checks.source: RULES 9.1 ('another phone number or an email')

checks.name: contact_changes_code_proof
checks.source: D75; D77 ('One rule everywhere'); D100; FS section 8

checks.name: contact_changes_by_whom
checks.source: D75 ('the request counts only from the customer's own chat'); D77 (staff at the desk); RULES 9.3; S11-20

checks.name: contact_changes_desk_has_business
checks.expression: way not in ('in_person', 'owner_team_edit') or business_id is not null

indexes.name: contact_changes_person_idx
indexes.why: A person's contact history: the 'don't text me' proof (FS line 756) and 'Contact details changed.' (RULES 9.3).
